title: Postmortem: Canary model weight corruption causing inference errors
summary: During a routine canary rollout of v2025.01.model-alpha to the /generate endpoint, a subset of canary pods started returning decoding errors and 500 responses. The root cause was a corrupted weights artifact that was incompatible with the tokenizer metadata in the model registry. The issue surfaced within the first 30 minutes of canary traffic and was rolled back by SRE and model ops within 45 minutes. Customer-facing impact was small (0.8% of requests during the canary window) but we observed noisy alerts and partial degradation for internal teams using the preview route.
impact: Errors (HTTP 500) and invalid decoded outputs for ~0.8% of total traffic routed to canary. No data leak or PII exposure. Some internal SDK users experienced corrupted outputs; external production customers were not on canary and unaffected.
detection: Automated canary health checks flagged increased 500s and tokenization-decoding exceptions. Observability alarms: route-error-rate > 1% for 5m, model-serve-latency p95 spike. On-call received paged alert at 2025-01-14T09:12:24Z.

root_cause: A corruption bit in the model weight artifact (introduced during artifact packaging step in model CI) produced a tensor layout mismatch at runtime. The model registry metadata listed tokenizer version tok-v2.1, but the new weight binary expected an updated tokenizer layout tok-v2.2. The mismatch produced out-of-vocab decoding errors at the serving runtime which bubbled up as 500s in the canary pods. The artifact checksum verification in CI was present but incorrectly validated against the staging bucket (race condition), allowing a partially written file to be promoted.
mitigation_steps:
1) Immediate: Paused canary promotion and rolled back canary routing to v2024.12.
2) Scaled down and restarted affected canary pods to clear KV caches.
3) Disabled batching on canary pool to reduce aggregated failure surface while debugging.
4) Marked artifact as quarantined in model registry and revoked promotion tokens.
5) Notified model-owners and security for artifact provenance verification.
rollback_playbook:
- Identify canary deployment name and current revision: kubectl -n inference get deploy -l role=model-canary
- Roll back to most recent stable revision or promote previous model: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=<REV> OR redwoodctl model rollback --model-id model-alpha --to-version v2024.12
- Force drain canary nodes gracefully: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Invalidate KV/prefix caches: redwoodctl cache invalidate --model model-alpha --scope canary
- Re-enable batching only after all health checks green for 30m: redwoodctl config set model-alpha batching.enabled true --env canary
- Update incident channel with status and ETA for full recovery
Note: If artifacts are suspected corrupted, do not re-promote until artifact checksums, tokenizer hashes, and model-registry entries are reconciled.
postmortem_actions:
- Short term (within 2 weeks): Add artifact write-commit confirmation to model CI and ensure promotion only reads from final bucket. (Owner: Model Ops)
- Medium term (30d): Implement cross-check gate between model weights and tokenizer manifest: require matching tokenizer hash in model artifact metadata and automated decode smoke test during release. (Owner: Research/Applied ML + Model Ops)
- Long term (90d): Add model artifact immutability policy and server-side checksum validation at serving runtime; add end-to-end CI smoke test that launches a lightweight canary container and runs 100 sample prompts. (Owners: ServRuntime + CI)
runbook_drafts:
Draft updates to the SRE runbook for model rollouts:
- Pre-promotion checklist: artifact checksum validated, tokenizer-hash match, integration smoke test passed, registry metadata sanity check, canary pool size defined.
- Canary monitoring: define specific SLOs (error-rate < 0.5%, p95 latency within 20% of baseline) and automatic pause triggers.
- Post-rollback diagnostics: commands to collect core dumps, model artifact hash, and tokenizer manifest; add standard log-grep expressions for 'decode error' and 'tensor size mismatch'
- Escalation matrix: Model Ops -> Applied ML -> SRE -> Eng on-call escalation times/contacts.
(See 'runbook: model-rollout-checklist' in Confluence for full template)
oncall_notes:
- What I ran during the incident: kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c model-serve | grep -i 'decode' ; redwoodctl model list --filter canary ; redwoodctl model info --model-id model-alpha --version v2025.01 ; aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-models --key alpha/v2025.01/model.pt --version-id <ver>
- Quick checks for responders: verify model registry tokenizer_hash matches artifact tokenizer_hash; run local decode with python snippet (attached in Confluence) before promoting; avoid mass scale promotions until smoke test; when in doubt, rollback and mark artifact quarantined.
- Communication: opened incident channel #inc-canary-mw1, updated status page stub, and informed Product about the rollback. Drafted customer note template for affected internal-preview users.
